title: Accuracy of prostate cancer screening recommendations for high-risk populations on YouTube and TikTok
screen_reason: Content analysis of the top 50 'prostate cancer screening' videos on YouTube and on TikTok, in which three reviewers rated each video against American Urological Association and National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines on a 5-point scale responding to 'this video does not contain misinformation'. The paper reports a share of videos per platform with moderate-to-high levels of misinformation (88% YouTube, 100% TikTok) and the complementary share deemed accurate (12% / 0%). Guideline concordance stated as accurate/inaccurate is an admissible CONTENT ground truth, so the two misinformation shares are CONTENT rows, both flagged borderline (see notes). The DISCERN/PEMAT results are QUALITY and are carried as QUALITY rows only.

estimates.country: Not stated (English-language videos, US authors, US guidelines)
estimates.measure_type: % of top-50 YouTube 'prostate cancer screening' videos rated as having moderate to high levels of misinformation against AUA/NCCN guidelines
estimates.denominator: 50 YouTube videos returned by the search term 'prostate cancer screening' that met inclusion criteria
estimates.definition: Video did NOT receive a mean reviewer score of Likert >=4 on the statement 'this video does not contain misinformation' relative to at least one set of guidelines; the paper reports the complement of the 12% deemed accurate as 'moderate to high levels of misinformation'
estimates.misinfo_def: 'this video does not contain misinformation', when compared to the most recent guidelines set forth by the American Urological Association (AUA) and the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN)
estimates.source_quote: A total of 98% of YT videos and 100% of TK videos had low- to moderate-quality consumer health information, and 88% of YT videos and 100% of TK videos had moderate to high levels of misinformation based on screening guidelines.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results (p. 206); corroborated by Table 2 'Mean Likert score >=4, n (%): 6 (12)' p. 211
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Three physician/medical-student reviewers (M.A., N.F., D.J.) independently scored every video on a 5-point Likert scale adapted from a previously published study, against AUA and NCCN prostate cancer screening guidelines; scores averaged across the three reviewers. No kappa or other inter-rater reliability statistic is reported for the misinformation scale.
estimates.moderator_quote: On 12 August 2021, a cookie-free, cache-cleared, incognito Safari browser was used to obtain the top 50 videos for the search term 'prostate cancer screening' on both YT and TK.
estimates.notes: Borderline because the instrument is a graded agreement scale rather than a false/true verdict: a video that states nothing untrue but simply omits guideline content (a patient story, a comedy clip) can score low and thus fall into the 88%. The authors themselves attribute much of the YouTube figure to videos being outdated rather than wrong. Value taken verbatim from the abstract, not computed as 100 - 12.

estimates.country: Not stated (English-language videos, US authors, US guidelines)
estimates.measure_type: % of top-50 TikTok 'prostate cancer screening' videos rated as having moderate to high levels of misinformation against AUA/NCCN guidelines
estimates.denominator: 50 TikTok videos returned by the search term 'prostate cancer screening' that met inclusion criteria
estimates.definition: No TikTok video reached a mean reviewer score of Likert >=4 on 'this video does not contain misinformation' relative to AUA or NCCN guidelines (Table 2: Mean Likert score >=4, TikTok 0 (0%))
estimates.misinfo_def: 'this video does not contain misinformation', when compared to the most recent guidelines set forth by the American Urological Association (AUA) and the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN)
estimates.source_quote: A total of 98% of YT videos and 100% of TK videos had low- to moderate-quality consumer health information, and 88% of YT videos and 100% of TK videos had moderate to high levels of misinformation based on screening guidelines.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results (p. 206); corroborated by Table 2 'Mean Likert score >=4, n (%): TikTok 0 (0)' p. 211
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same three reviewers, same 5-point Likert scale against AUA and NCCN guidelines, mean of three scores. Mean AUA Likert on TikTok 1.113 (SD 0.354) and mean NCCN Likert 1.107 (SD 0.333). No inter-rater reliability statistic reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: On 12 August 2021, a cookie-free, cache-cleared, incognito Safari browser was used to obtain the top 50 videos for the search term 'prostate cancer screening' on both YT and TK.
estimates.notes: Same borderline caveat as the YouTube row, and it bites harder here: 26% of the TikTok videos are patient stories and 10% comedy, which cannot be guideline-concordant by construction, so the 100% figure is substantially an omission measure rather than a count of false claims.

estimates.source_quote: A total of 98% of YT videos and 100% of TK videos had low- to moderate-quality consumer health information, and 88% of YT videos and 100% of TK videos had moderate to high levels of misinformation based on screening guidelines.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) the pooled cross-platform figures in section 3.3 ('few videos across both platforms had good support for shared decision-making (14%), and even fewer were deemed either sufficiently accurate (6%) or high quality (1%)') - these pool the two platforms and duplicate the per-platform rows already taken, so keeping them would double-count; (b) the individual DISCERN component and PEMAT sub-scores (risks 22%/0%, benefits 20%/0%, shared decision-making 28%/0%, understandability 26%/2%, actionability 22%/0%) - quality components, redundant with the composite QUALITY rows; (c) the 'Mean Likert score >=4' cells (YT 12%, TK 0%) - the accurate complement of the CONTENT rows, not a second estimate; (d) mean AUA/NCCN Likert scores (2.293, 2.140 for YT; 1.113, 1.107 for TK) - scale means with no share, no row per the rule; (e) all racial/ethnic representation and content-topic percentages - not veracity measures; (f) the sub-analysis of YouTube videos with vs without Black/Hispanic representation (accurate: 0% vs 7%) - a demographic subgroup split, not the paper's headline. Internal inconsistency to flag: Table 1 gives White representation as '44 (98)' and Black as '5 (10)' out of 50 YouTube videos, but 44/50 is 88%, not 98%; the text also says 'YT: 98%' for White speakers, so the count 44 and the percentage 98 cannot both be right. This does not affect the extracted rows.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis of the top 50 videos for 'prostate cancer screening' on YouTube and on TikTok, retrieved 12 August 2021 in a cookie-free, cache-cleared incognito browser; 62 YouTube and 75 TikTok videos were screened to reach 50 each (non-English, no audio, duplicate, unrelated and >12-minute videos excluded). Three reviewers independently scored every video on DISCERN, the audiovisual PEMAT, and a 5-point misinformation Likert against AUA and NCCN guidelines, with scores averaged; perceived race/ethnicity by majority vote of the three. No inter-rater reliability coefficient is reported for any instrument. Single search day, single country of guidelines, English only.
rob.item6_quote: To assess accuracy of information, a 5-point Likert scale adapted from previously published studies (1 = strongly disagree; 5 = strongly agree) was used to respond to the statement, 'this video does not contain misinformation', when compared to the most recent guidelines set forth by the American Urological Association (AUA) and the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN).
rob.item10_quote: A total of 98% of YT videos and 100% of TK videos had low- to moderate-quality consumer health information, and 88% of YT videos and 100% of TK videos had moderate to high levels of misinformation based on screening guidelines.
